items.description: Analyze repository structure and document existing infrastructure
items.acceptance_criteria: Written document (repo_analysis.md) listing all modules (.archivara/semantic_scholar.py, TASK_orchestrator.md, figures/, results/), their purposes, data flow between agents (orchestrator, researcher, writer, reviewer), and identified gaps (no graph code, no SAT integration, no test infrastructure)

items.description: Conduct comprehensive literature review on Hadwiger-Nelson problem and unit-distance graph constructions
items.acceptance_criteria: Search web and Semantic Scholar for papers on: (1) de Grey 2018 original construction, (2) Polymath16 simplification threads, (3) Heule SAT-based minimization, (4) Parts 509-vertex record, (5) Exoo-Ismailescu alternative constructions, (6) Pritikin/Parts lower bounds on 6-chromatic graph size (6993), (7) Mundinger et al. 2024 six-colorings via neural discovery, (8) Cranston-Rabern fractional chromatic number, (9) strip-coloring SAT approaches, (10) two-distance and multi-distance graph results. At least 15 relevant papers identified with full bibliographic details

items.description: Create and populate sources.bib with BibTeX entries for all consulted sources
items.acceptance_criteria: sources.bib in repo root contains valid BibTeX entries for at least 15 papers including: deGrey2018 (chromatic number >= 5), Heule2019 (computing small unit-distance graphs), Parts2020 (small 6-chromatic two-distance graph), Pritikin1998 (all UDG of order 6197 are 6-colorable), MundingerEtAl2024 (extending six-colorings), CranstonRabern2015 (fractional chromatic number), ExooIsmailescu2022 (constructing 5-chromatic UDGs), Polymath2018 (Hadwiger-Nelson simplification), HeuleOostema2023 (strip coloring via SAT), and at least 6 additional relevant sources. Each entry has author, title, year, and venue fields

items.description: Analyze de Grey's gadget composition methodology in detail
items.acceptance_criteria: Technical document (degrey_analysis.md) covering: (1) the Moser spindle (7 vertices, 11 edges, chi=4) and Golomb graph as base gadgets, (2) the H graph (7 hexagonal lattice points), (3) the L graph (121 vertices from 4 overlaid hexagonal lattice portions), (4) the V/W/N composition chain yielding 20425 -> 1581 vertices, (5) the spindling operation and its algebraic meaning, (6) the role of the ring Z[omega, sqrt(3), sqrt(11)] where omega = e^{i*pi/3}, (7) why 4-colorings are thwarted by spindling distance 2 about 0. Must cite at least 5 specific papers from sources.bib

items.description: Survey known lower bounds on size of potential 6-chromatic unit-distance graphs and feasibility constraints
items.acceptance_criteria: Document (feasibility_analysis.md) summarizing: (1) Pritikin's proof that all UDGs with <= 6197 vertices are 6-colorable, (2) Parts' improvement to 6993 vertices, (3) implications for minimum graph size needed (~7000+ vertices), (4) comparison with de Grey's 1581 for chi=5 vs Pritikin's 12 for chi=4, (5) computational complexity estimates for SAT solving at 7000+ vertices with 5 colors, (6) assessment of Polymath16 thread 3 ('Is 6-chromatic within reach?') conclusions, (7) survey of approaches that failed or showed limitations. Must reference specific prior work from sources.bib

items.description: Catalog all known 5-chromatic gadgets and their structural properties for use as building blocks
items.acceptance_criteria: Structured catalog (gadget_catalog.json) listing at least 8 gadgets: Moser spindle (7v, chi=4), Golomb graph (10v, chi=4), de Grey's H graph (7v), de Grey's L graph (121v), Parts' 509-vertex graph, Heule's 553-vertex graph, Exoo-Ismailescu alternative base graphs, and the 6-chromatic 79-vertex graph in R^3 from Polymath16. Each entry must include vertex count, edge count, chromatic number, key structural properties (symmetry group, algebraic ring of coordinates), and citation from sources.bib

items.description: Implement core unit-distance graph data structure and exact arithmetic coordinate system
items.acceptance_criteria: Python module (src/graph.py) implementing: (1) UnitDistanceGraph class storing points as exact algebraic coordinates (using sympy or custom ring arithmetic over Z[omega, sqrt(3), sqrt(5), sqrt(11)]), (2) automatic edge detection via exact distance-1 computation, (3) adjacency list representation, (4) methods for vertex/edge count, degree sequence, connected components, (5) serialization to/from JSON. All unit tests pass (tests/test_graph.py with >= 10 test cases)

items.description: Implement SAT-based k-coloring solver with UNSAT certificate verification
items.acceptance_criteria: Python module (src/sat_coloring.py) implementing: (1) encoding of k-coloring as CNF (at-least-one-color and at-most-one-color per vertex, different-color for each edge), (2) integration with pysat (or python-sat) supporting Glucose4 and CaDiCaL backends, (3) function is_k_colorable(graph, k) returning (bool, coloring_or_None), (4) DRAT proof output for UNSAT results, (5) timing and clause-count metrics. Verified against known results: Moser spindle is 4-chromatic (3-coloring UNSAT, 4-coloring SAT), Golomb graph is 4-chromatic, K3 is 3-chromatic

items.description: Reproduce de Grey's 509-vertex 5-chromatic unit-distance graph and verify with SAT solver
items.acceptance_criteria: Script (src/reproduce_degrey.py) that: (1) constructs the 509-vertex Parts graph (or de Grey's 1581-vertex original) from published coordinates, (2) verifies all edges are exactly unit distance, (3) confirms 4-coloring is UNSAT via SAT solver (with timing reported), (4) confirms 5-coloring is SAT, (5) outputs the graph to results/degrey_baseline.json. SAT solver must return UNSAT for k=4 within 60 seconds on the 509-vertex graph

items.description: Implement gadget composition operations: union, rotation, spindling, and lattice overlay
items.acceptance_criteria: Python module (src/composition.py) implementing: (1) graph_union(G1, G2) merging two UDGs with shared vertices identified by coordinate equality, (2) rotate(G, center, angle) producing a rotated copy, (3) spindle(G, d, center) performing the spindling operation at distance d, (4) lattice_overlay(G, lattice_points) centering copies of G at each lattice point, (5) truncate(G, center, radius) removing vertices beyond radius. Each operation preserves exact arithmetic. At least 8 unit tests verifying correctness against known small examples

items.description: Implement graph analysis metrics: spindle count, clique number, fractional chromatic number bound, independence number
items.acceptance_criteria: Python module (src/metrics.py) implementing: (1) count_moser_spindles(G) counting Moser spindle subgraph occurrences, (2) clique_number(G) via greedy + exact for small graphs, (3) fractional_chromatic_lower_bound(G) using LP relaxation, (4) independence_number(G) via SAT encoding, (5) density metrics (edges/vertices ratio, average degree). Verified on Moser spindle: clique_number=3, fractional_chi >= 3.5. Results logged to results/metrics_baseline.json

items.description: Design and implement a 5-chromatic gadget library with tight coloring constraints for use as building blocks toward 6-chromaticity
items.acceptance_criteria: Module (src/gadget_library.py) containing: (1) at least 5 distinct 5-chromatic unit-distance subgraphs with vertex counts between 100-1000, each verified via SAT, (2) for each gadget: documentation of which vertex subsets are forced to share colors in any 5-coloring (constraint propagation analysis via partial SAT), (3) identification of 'interface vertices' suitable for composition, (4) a function forced_color_constraints(gadget, k=5) that returns which vertex pairs must be same-color or different-color in every valid k-coloring. Constraints verified against exhaustive enumeration for at least the 2 smallest gadgets

items.description: Implement hierarchical gadget composition strategy following de Grey's methodology scaled to 5-chromatic base
items.acceptance_criteria: Module (src/hierarchical_builder.py) implementing: (1) Level-0: 5-chromatic base gadgets from gadget_library, (2) Level-1: compose L-graphs by overlaying rotated copies of base gadgets to force monochromatic triples in 5-colorings, (3) Level-2: compose W-graphs by centering L-graph copies at base gadget vertices and truncating, (4) Level-3: full composition centering W-copies at hexagonal lattice points, (5) at each level, SAT-verify the composed graph's chromatic number (expecting monotonic increase in hardness). Must produce at least 3 candidate graphs at Level-2 with >= 5000 vertices each, with 5-coloring SAT difficulty metrics reported

items.description: Implement algebraic ring exploration to discover optimal coordinate rings for 6-chromatic constructions
items.acceptance_criteria: Module (src/ring_explorer.py) implementing: (1) systematic generation of unit-distance graphs over rings Z[omega, sqrt(p1), ..., sqrt(pk)] for various prime sets, (2) edge density computation for each ring, (3) spindle density computation, (4) automated search for rings yielding high spindle/vertex ratios (de Grey's key insight was high spindle density), (5) comparison table of at least 10 distinct rings with their maximum achieved chromatic number, spindle density, and graph sizes. Output to results/ring_exploration.json. Must explore rings beyond de Grey's Z[omega, sqrt(3), sqrt(11)] to include sqrt(5), sqrt(7), sqrt(13), and combinations

items.description: Implement neural-guided search for gadget configurations inspired by Mundinger et al. 2024 deep annealing approach
items.acceptance_criteria: Module (src/neural_search.py) implementing: (1) differentiable loss function encoding coloring conflicts as soft constraints (following Mundinger et al. ICML 2025 formulation), (2) gradient-based optimization of point positions in R^2 to maximize coloring hardness, (3) annealing schedule transitioning from continuous relaxation to discrete coloring, (4) integration with SAT solver for exact verification of candidates found by neural search, (5) at least 100 candidate graphs generated and SAT-verified per run. Must cite Mundinger et al. 2024 methodology. Output best candidates to results/neural_candidates/

items.description: Implement SAT-based graph pruning and minimization pipeline following Heule's clausal proof minimization method
items.acceptance_criteria: Module (src/pruning.py) implementing: (1) iterative vertex deletion: for each vertex, check if removal preserves chromatic number via SAT, (2) clausal proof analysis: use DRAT proof structure to identify critical vertices/edges, (3) vertex replacement: substitute subsets with smaller equivalent subgraphs, (4) symmetry-breaking clauses to accelerate SAT solving on symmetric graphs, (5) parallel pruning with configurable worker count. Must reduce a test 5-chromatic graph (e.g., de Grey 1581) by at least 10% while preserving 5-chromaticity. Cite Heule 2019 methodology

items.description: Implement multi-distance and spindling-based composition specifically targeting 6-chromaticity barriers
items.acceptance_criteria: Module (src/multi_distance.py) implementing: (1) two-distance graph construction (unit distance + secondary distance d), leveraging Parts' 6-chromatic two-distance results, (2) systematic search over secondary distances d in [0.35, 0.66] (the range from Mundinger et al. 2024 where 6-colorings are tight), (3) spindling at multiple distances simultaneously, (4) composition of two-distance gadgets into unit-distance-only graphs via geometric embedding tricks, (5) at least 20 candidate compositions generated with SAT verification. Must produce graphs where 5-coloring SAT solving takes measurably longer than baseline 5-chromatic graphs (quantified by clause count and solver time)

items.description: Execute systematic composition experiments combining all Phase 3 approaches at scale
items.acceptance_criteria: Script (experiments/run_compositions.py) that: (1) generates at least 50 candidate graphs using hierarchical composition (item_013), ring exploration (item_014), and neural search (item_015), (2) each candidate has >= 7000 vertices (above Parts' 6993 lower bound), (3) runs 5-coloring SAT on each with 1-hour timeout, (4) logs for each: vertex count, edge count, spindle count, SAT result (SAT/UNSAT/TIMEOUT), solve time, clause count, (5) results saved to results/composition_experiments.csv. At least 5 candidates must complete SAT solving (not timeout)

items.description: Evaluate SAT solver performance across multiple solvers and encodings on largest candidate graphs
items.acceptance_criteria: Script (experiments/sat_benchmark.py) that: (1) tests at least 3 SAT solvers (Glucose4, CaDiCaL, Kissat) on the top-10 hardest candidates from item_018, (2) tests at least 2 encodings (direct encoding, log encoding for colors), (3) applies symmetry-breaking preprocessing, (4) records and compares solve times, peak memory, conflict counts, (5) identifies if any candidate is UNSAT for 5-coloring across all solvers. Results in results/sat_benchmark.csv with statistical summary

items.description: If any 5-coloring UNSAT result is found, independently verify and minimize the graph
items.acceptance_criteria: Script (experiments/verify_and_minimize.py) that for any UNSAT candidate: (1) re-verifies with at least 2 independent SAT solvers, (2) obtains DRAT proof certificate, (3) validates DRAT proof with drat-trim, (4) runs Heule-style minimization from item_016 to find smallest subgraph preserving 6-chromaticity, (5) exports final minimal graph with exact coordinates to results/six_chromatic_graph.json, (6) generates visual embedding plot saved to figures/six_chromatic_embedding.png. If no UNSAT found, document the closest results (hardest instances by solve time/clause count) and analyze what structural properties correlate with hardness

items.description: Analyze coloring structure of near-miss candidates to identify why 5-colorings survive
items.acceptance_criteria: Script (experiments/coloring_analysis.py) that for the top-10 hardest SAT instances from item_018: (1) extracts all 5-colorings (or a sample if too many) from the SAT solver, (2) analyzes color class sizes and symmetry, (3) identifies bottleneck regions where coloring is most constrained, (4) computes for each vertex: number of valid color assignments across all solutions, (5) visualizes constraint heatmaps saved to figures/constraint_heatmaps/. Report (results/coloring_analysis.md) identifying the most promising structural modifications to push toward UNSAT

items.description: Compare experimental results against prior work benchmarks from literature review
items.acceptance_criteria: Comparison table (results/prior_work_comparison.md) containing: (1) de Grey's original 1581-vertex graph metrics vs our reproduced baseline, (2) Parts' 509-vertex graph metrics, (3) Heule's minimized 553-vertex graph metrics, (4) our best candidate graphs' metrics side-by-side, (5) fractional chromatic number bounds compared to Cranston-Rabern, (6) edge/vertex density compared across all graphs, (7) SAT solve time scaling analysis. Must reference at least 8 specific papers from sources.bib. Include assessment of whether our candidates exceed the difficulty frontier of known 5-chromatic graphs

items.description: Write comprehensive technical report documenting methodology, results, and analysis
items.acceptance_criteria: Report (results/technical_report.md) with sections: (1) Introduction and problem statement with historical context, (2) Methodology covering all Phase 3 approaches, (3) Experimental results from Phase 4 with tables and figures, (4) Analysis of why candidates succeeded or fell short, (5) Comparison with prior work citing at least 10 papers from sources.bib, (6) Lessons learned about structural properties correlated with high chromatic number, (7) Concrete next steps and open questions. Minimum 3000 words

items.description: Generate publication-quality visualizations of key results
items.acceptance_criteria: At least 6 figures saved to figures/ including: (1) graph embedding of best candidate with vertices colored by constraint tightness, (2) scaling plot: vertex count vs SAT solve time for all candidates, (3) ring comparison chart from item_014, (4) composition hierarchy diagram showing gadget assembly, (5) bar chart comparing our candidates to prior work benchmarks, (6) if UNSAT found: the 6-chromatic graph with a valid 6-coloring displayed. All figures in PNG format at >= 300 DPI with labeled axes and legends

items.description: Create reproducibility package with all code, data, and instructions
items.acceptance_criteria: Updated README.md with: (1) project overview and mathematical background, (2) installation instructions (dependencies: sympy, python-sat, networkx, matplotlib, numpy), (3) step-by-step reproduction guide for all experiments, (4) description of repository structure, (5) results summary with key findings. requirements.txt listing all Python dependencies with pinned versions. All scripts runnable from repo root with documented command-line interfaces

items.description: Conduct final review: validate all results, check for errors, and assess scientific contribution
items.acceptance_criteria: Review checklist (results/review_checklist.md) confirming: (1) all SAT results independently verified with >= 2 solvers, (2) all unit-distance claims verified by exact arithmetic (no floating-point), (3) sources.bib contains >= 15 entries with complete fields, (4) all figures are reproducible from provided scripts, (5) technical report accurately reflects experimental data, (6) explicit statement of whether chi(R^2) >= 6 was achieved or what the closest result was, (7) honest assessment of contribution relative to state of the art (Parts 6993 lower bound, de Grey/Heule/Parts methods)
